The parameters $ \langle C^P(k) \rangle_1, \langle C^M_1(k) \rangle_1 $ and $ \langle C^M_2(k) \rangle_1 $ are then calculated according to Section III-A. After solving (23) and obtaining the $ \hat{\xi}_{\text{Sol}} $, we save it as $ \hat{\xi}_{\text{SAveLast}} $, obtain the iteration error, and make $ \hat{\xi}_{\text{Sol}} $ as the initial value for next iteration. In addition, we define the error as the distance between current solution $ \hat{\xi}_{\text{Sol}} $ and previous solution $ \hat{\xi}_{\text{SAveLast}} $. The iteration continues until the error is less than a predefined error threshold (threshold) or a maximum number of iterations (maxIter) is reached. The details are in Algorithm 1. Upon successfully solving a single optimization window, we can continue the process and solve for the overall simulation time using a vintage MPC routine.

IV. NUMERICAL TESTS

In this section, we present a simple simulation example to illustrate the applicability of the GP-based MPC formulation for WDN operations. The considered water network is an 8-node network from EPANET Users Manual [17, Chapter 2]. The numerical tests are simulated using EPANET Matlab Toolkit [20] with GP solver GGP-LAB [21]. The basic parameters in 8-node network including the elevation of nodes, length, and diameter of pipes are obtained from [17].
